Living near a school does not mean a place at it. Your child's school comes from the district's catchment boundaries, and those change, so confirm the address with the district before you write an offer.
Source: BC Ministry of Education and Child Care school list (2025/26, updated July 2026) and the Province's post-secondary locations list. Neighbourhood placement is from our own area research.
Parkcrest homes listed and sold, June to September 2026

Parkcrest, September 2026. Detached houses: 25 listed at month end and 3 sold in September, a sales ratio of 12% (a balanced market). No condos and townhomes were listed or sold in Parkcrest between June and September.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 9 sold over 4 months against an average of 28.5 listed, about 12.7 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 3 sold.

items.t: Simon Fraser University Area real estate

faq.a: In north Burnaby between Hastings Street and Lougheed Highway, around Kensington Avenue and Halifax Street, named for Parkcrest Elementary at 6055 Halifax St; it is a GVR MLS® sub-area within the City of Burnaby.

faq.q: Are there condos or townhomes in Parkcrest?
faq.a: Not in the September 2026 data — the SnapStats row for Parkcrest shows 0 condos and townhomes listed and 0 sold, against 25 detached listings and 3 detached solds, so the area traded as a detached-house neighbourhood that month (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which schools serve a Parkcrest address?
faq.a: It depends on the address. In-area SD41 schools include Parkcrest Elementary (K–7), 6055 Halifax St, and Lochdale Community Elementary (K–7), 6990 Aubrey Street, with Burnaby North Secondary (8–12) to the west; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.

Kensington Complex has an NHL regulation ice rink with 620 permanent seats, used for hockey and figure skating in winter and lacrosse in summer, and Kensington Park is listed with 3 tennis and 3 pickleball courts; the complex was closed for the summer for roof repairs, with ice returning September 8.
